title: Вторая порция рулетиков  (A Second Helping of Rolls)

segments.t: Furious that Senya and Fedya kidnapped a reporter, Nagiyev heads out with them to fix the mess before the police get involved. Meanwhile in the kitchen, Nastya tells Max that the vegetarian guest loved the morning dish so much he ordered a second helping.
Заказал такие же рулетики, как в прошлый раз.
Нет, я сам очень есть хочу.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Dmitry Vladimirovich.' The meaning hinges on 'Dmitry' working together with 'Vladimirovich' in spoken Russian.
'No, no.' Notice how Russian expresses 'there is no' and 'there is no' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'We will go together.' Fedya anchors the line on 'together', while 'will be off' completes the thought.
'And I will be the one held responsible later.' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'to answer' without extra filler words.
'Well, it is the vegetarian.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'vegetarian'. Fedya answers right away.
Заказал такие же рулетики, как в прошлый раз.
'He ordered the exact same rolls as last time.' The grammar packs 'ordered' and 'time' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'The vegetarian. He ordered the exact same rolls.' Max brings out the contrast between 'vegetarian' and 'ordered' in a few short words.
'So this order is on you.' Notice how Russian expresses 'like this' and 'you' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'It will turn out to be a proper vegetarian dish.' In Russian, the idea of 'normal' flows naturally into 'will come out' without extra filler words.
'Stop feeding the man meat for free.' Notice how Russian expresses 'enough' and 'to feed' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Нет, я сам очень есть хочу.
'No, I am very hungry myself.' Chef Barinov pairs 'very much' with 'want' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
'Oh, alright, alright.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'really?!' without extra filler words.
'Here, compliments of the chef.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'on' before landing on 'chef'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Заказал такие же рулетики, как в прошлый раз.
Нет, я сам очень есть хочу.

That wraps up this scene as nagiyev goes out with Senya and Fedya to deal with the captive, while the vegetarian guest returns to Claude Monet and orders the exact same rolls from Max. See you next time!
